title: causal Mirror-MQA
hypothesis: Causal decoding with one physical MQA K/V cache and vectorized per-query-head Mirror views can recover a shared-view four-head teacher without expanding persistent cache state; MQA/GQA and full MHA bound quality and cache bandwidth.
physical_object: one causal K/V projection pair and one shared persistent cache stream
mirror_coordinate: vectorized pairwise rotations over four-dimensional cached K/V channels, one angle per pair and query head
logical_multiplicity: four query heads with distinct K/V views of one physical MQA cache

task.attention: causal self-attention with shared output projection

teacher_modes.shared_causal_kv: one K/V projection pair plus per-head rotations, causal mask
teacher_modes.independent_causal_kv: four independent K/V pairs, causal mask

task.storage_metric: serialized model bytes, exact persistent cache bytes per sequence, and cache-read proxy

controls: MQA cache plus vectorized Mirror views

development.selection_metric: mean held-out causal output MSE pooled across methods and modes

storage.authority: actual serialized full inference payload bytes and exact float32 KV tensor bytes
storage.cache_formula: 2 * physical KV heads * head_dim * sequence length * 4 bytes

success_gate: In all three fresh shared-causal-KV worlds, Mirror output MSE <=1.10x full MHA, model+cache bytes < full MHA, and it beats MQA at equal cache bytes with no worse combined storage/compute. Report bandwidth and CPU runtime separately.
failure_gate: Mirror misses output quality in two or more fresh shared-view worlds, or MQA/GQA has equal/lower total storage and compute with equal/better quality. Independent-KV failure alone is a structural boundary.
boundaries: teacher intentionally uses the same vectorized rotation family
cache bandwidth is a proxy, not GPU hardware measurement
fixed update screen, not language/capacity claim
